title: PreToolUse shell guard: block git revert -q / revert+--amend and zsh non-splitting variable expansions
description: User ruling 2026-09-25 (AskUserQuestion, this session): add a hook. Two mistakes recurred on 2026-09-25 with memory notes loaded that describe them exactly: (1) 'git revert --no-edit HEAD -q' fails (revert has no -q), and a following 'git commit --amend' in the same call rewrites the commit meant to be reverted (LCLI-588, caught only by a rejected push; first seen LCLI-539); (2) the Bash tool runs zsh, which does not word-split an unquoted parameter expansion: 'set -- $r' in a CI poll never broke its loop, and 'A="--actor ..."; quest ... $A' passed one argument. A note does not fire at the moment of writing; a PreToolUse hook does. Scope: a tracked .claude/hooks/shell-guard.ts (pure detector plus a stdin entry point that exits 2 with the safe form on stderr), a bun test with positive and negative cases, and registration in the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json (settings.json/settings.local.json are local-only by design, see .gitignore:78-82). Commands run under bash -c / sh -c are exempt from the zsh checks.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The guard rejects: git revert with -q/--quiet; git revert and --amend in one command; unquoted set -- $var; an unquoted $VAR whose assignment in the same command starts with a dash; for x in $var — and accepts the safe forms (${=var}, quoted use, bash -c wrapping, git revert alone)
A test proves each rejection and each acceptance, and a mutation of the detector turns a predicted subset red
The hook is registered locally and a live Bash call of a guarded shape is refused by it in this session

finalSummary: .claude/hooks/shell-guard.ts (tracked) refuses, as a PreToolUse hook on Bash, six shapes: git revert -q/--quiet; git revert with --amend in one command; unquoted set -- $var; for x in $var; an unquoted $VAR holding flags (value starts with a dash); a multi-word $VAR run as a command. Commands under bash -c / sh -c (any options before -c) are exempt from the zsh rules; '# shell-guard: allow' passes a command through; exit 2 with the rule and the safe form on stderr. test/shell-guard.test.ts: 10 refusals, 13 acceptances, 2 hook-process cases, 25/25 green; biome clean (file-level ignore for noTemplateCurlyInString, since the strings are shell syntax); tsc clean. Mutations, predicted from the case labels before running: disabling set-positional reddened exactly its 2 cases plus the hook-process case (3 of 25); removing the bash -c exemption reddened exactly the 2 bash -c acceptances. Registered in the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json (settings files are local-only by design, .gitignore:78-82), so a fresh clone must re-register it. Live proof in this session: 'x="a b"; set -- $x' was refused by the hook with the set-positional message, and the ${=x} form passed (2 positionals). Full bun test: 3469 pass; the only failures are publish-release-script.test.ts timeouts at 5000ms (exit 143) on this machine, a file this change does not touch.
